learningObjective: Identify which GPU generations support which quantized Tensor Core precisions and what falls back to software-emulated kernels.

canonicalClaims.claim: NVIDIA Tensor Core precision support by generation: INT8 on Turing+; FP16/BF16 on Turing+ (BF16 on Ampere+); FP8 on Ada (sm_89) and Hopper (sm_90). W4A16 kernels operate on Ampere+ by dequantizing INT4 weights to FP16/BF16 in registers and using the corresponding Tensor Core; no dedicated INT4 Tensor Core is required.
conditions: The framework has appropriate kernel implementations for the target precision.
nonImplications: Does not imply generational peak-TOPS is uniform.
Does not imply software-emulated fallback kernels deliver speedup.

misconceptions.claim: FP8 Tensor Cores are supported on Ampere via driver update.
misconceptions.whyWrong: FP8 Tensor Cores are new hardware; a driver cannot add them to Ampere.

misconceptions.claim: W4A16 requires INT4 Tensor Core hardware.
misconceptions.whyWrong: W4A16 kernels dequant INT4 to FP16/BF16 in registers and use FP16/BF16 Tensor Cores.

misconceptions.claim: Any kernel implementation for a target precision guarantees speedup over FP16.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Software-emulated fallback kernels on CUDA cores are often slower than FP16 Tensor Core kernels.

misconceptions.claim: H100 W4A16 is slower than A100 W4A16 because Hopper deprecated INT4 Tensor Cores.
misconceptions.whyWrong: W4A16 kernels do not use INT4 TCs; H100 W4A16 is typically faster due to higher FP16 TC throughput and bandwidth.

implementationFacts: cuBLAS Lt exposes INT8 GEMM via CUBLAS_COMPUTE_32I.
CUTLASS provides templated kernels for INT8, FP8, BF16, FP16, TF32.
Marlin and ExLlama INT4 kernels are custom W4A16 kernels not shipped with cuBLAS.
performanceScenarios: FP8 W8A8 on H100 achieves ~2× BF16 throughput; on A100 the same precision falls back to slower FP16 emulation.
